extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark covering 20 challenging video tasks for evaluating temporal understanding capabilities of MLLMs, with automatically generated multiple-choice QA from public video benchmarks.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li; Yali Wang; Yinan He; Yizhuo Li; Yi Wang; Yi Liu; Zun Wang; Jilan Xu; Guo Chen; Ping Luo; Limin Wang; Yu Qiao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was built by selecting videos from 11 existing public video datasets, filtering them for diversity, temporal sensitivity, and question difficulty, and automatically converting open-sourced video annotations into multiple-choice QA using LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos and annotations were collected from 11 public video benchmarks: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were filtered to improve diversity and temporal sensitivity by selecting 11 datasets, removing short clips with negligible motion and extremely long videos, keeping intermediate durations mainly from 5s to 35s, and applying task-specific filtering criteria for datasets such as STAR and CLEVRER.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were automatically generated as multiple-choice QA from public video annotations. ChatGPT was used to generate questions for videos based on task definitions, while answer options were constructed either from templates and ground-truth annotations or generated by ChatGPT for some tasks. Final answer options were sampled, shuffled, and length-balanced.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The benchmark uses multiple-choice format to ensure evaluation correctness and fairness and avoid biased scoring from LLM-based or human scoring of open-ended answers; answer options were also processed to avoid answer leakage by balancing option lengths.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note a minimal source gap between instruction data and MVBench because CLEVRER in instruction data has similar questions to some MVBench tasks, so evaluation is not strictly out-of-domain.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is not strictly out-of-domain due to overlap with CLEVRER-like questions in instruction data, and current MLLMs perform poorly on position, count, and character tasks, suggesting limited generalization without related tuning data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating the temporal understanding capabilities of MLLMs using multiple-choice QA across 20 video understanding tasks.

inLanguage.evidence: MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark

isLiveDataset.evidence: Ultimately, we produce 200 multiple-choice QA pairs for each temporal understanding task.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Specifically, we design an automatic QA generation paradigm in Fig. 2, which efficiently converts open-sourced video annotations into multiple-choice QAs for evaluating MLLMs.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Second, guided by the task definition, we design an automatic annotation paradigm to generate multiple-choice QAs for each task, by converting 11public video benchmarks with LLMs.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The videos are collected from the public datasets, including STAR [82], PAXION [79], Moments in Time V1 [57], FunQA [87], CLEVRER [95], Perception Test [61], Charades-STA [20], MoVQA [102], NTU RGB+D[48], VLN-CE [32] and TVQA [35].

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: To guarantee that each task is temporal sensitive, we eliminate short clips which generally contain negligible motions, and also delete extremely long videos which often present overly complicated contexts that are hard for evaluation. Hence, we select videos with intermediate duration, primarily ranging from 5s to 35s.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Specifically, we first use ChatGPT [58] to generate a question for each video, based on the task definition.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Note that, we use the multiple-choice format instead of the open-ended one, for evaluation correction and faimess.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Specifically, we first use ChatGPT [58] to generate a question for each video, based on the task definition.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Note that there is a minimal source gap between our instruction data and MVBench.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Specifically, the CLEVRER [95] in our instruction data has similar questions as Moving Attribute and Counterfactual Inference in MVBench, leading the evaluation is not strictly out-domain.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: MVBench , which aims at comprehensively evaluating the temporal perception capabilities of MLLMs in the open world.
